title: Enterprise Onboarding & Support Playbook - Integrations, Escalations, Known Issues, Health Checks and QBRs
author: Aisha Kumar
content:
Overview:

This playbook consolidates the standard operating procedures for enterprise onboarding at Redwood Inference, covering: integration guides for common setup patterns, escalation procedures for support issues, a curated list of known issues and short-term workarounds, support process (ticket lifecycle and SLAs), and recommended health-check and QBR materials. Intended audience: Customer Success Managers (CSMs), Support Engineers (L2), Solutions Engineers, and Customer Engineering contacts.

Goals:
- Reduce time-to-first-success for new enterprise customers
- Provide a consistent escalation path to resolve production incidents quickly
- Capture repeatable integration steps and known workarounds to accelerate troubleshooting
- Standardize health-checks and QBR content to drive proactive risk reduction

Scope:
- Applies to all Dedicated and Private deployment onboarding, and to higher-touch Hosted customers (> $X/month committed spend).
- Includes network, authentication, model pinning/rollout, observability, and common SDK/runtime issues.

Ownership and roles:
- CSM (primary owner): Customer relationship, scheduling QBRs, onboarding checklist completion.
- Solutions Engineer (SE): Leads initial integration, API/SDK verification, and custom work.
- Support L2 / Platform Engineer: Incident response and root-cause analysis when escalated.
- Eng on-call (runtime/infra): Invoked for production outages per escalation matrix.

Onboarding checklist (high level):
1) Kickoff (week 0):
   - Introductions (CSM, SE, customer's engineering lead).
   - Share onboarding plan and success criteria.
2) Access & Network (days 0-3):
   - Exchange service account details and verify SSO/KMS if required.
   - For Private deployment: validate VPC peering, firewall rules, and route tables.
   - Checklist item: run curl test to control plane endpoint and confirm TLS chain.
     Example: curl -v https://api.redwood.example.com/health --header 'Authorization: Bearer <token>'
3) Authentication & Secrets (days 1-4):
   - Verify API token scopes, rotate demo tokens, and onboard KMS keys (if customer-managed).
4) Model & Performance Baseline (days 2-7):
   - Pin model versions for critical routes and run a perf suite (10k tokens across target input distribution).
   - Capture baseline latency and TPS in the onboarding dashboard.
5) Observability & Alerts (days 3-10):
   - Ensure traces and metrics are streaming to the customer console and any external SIEM (if applicable).
   - Configure primary alert: downstream error rate > 2% for 5m or 95th percentile latency breach > SLO.
6) End-to-end validation (before handoff):
   - Run sample requests for all critical routes and confirm expected output quality and latency.
   - Sign-off (CSM + customer engineering) for move to BAU.

Integration guide (common patterns):
- REST SDK quicktest: run a lightweight generation against customer model and ensure streaming is functional.
- Embeddings integration: batch embed pipeline sample (500 docs) and validate vector store ingestion.
- Function/tool call verification: provide signed sample request payloads and test fallbacks using the sandbox tool.
- On-prem notes: ensure CUDA drivers (>= 12.x) and compatible NCCL versions are present. For quantized models, confirm libsupport-quant v1.2+ is installed.

Escalation playbook (summary):
- Severity definitions:
  - Sev1 (Critical): Production outage (> 50% customers impacted or critical customer downtime). Response: immediate page to eng-sre, oncall runtime, and CS leader.
  - Sev2 (High): Partial degradation impacting SLAs for a single enterprise (e.g., high latency or increased errors). Response: notify Support L2 and SE; begin triage within 30 minutes.
  - Sev3 (Medium): Functionality loss for non-critical routes or reproducible bugs with workaround. Response: triage during business hours and track in bug backlog.
  - Sev4 (Low): Documentation/UX requests or cosmetic issues.

Escalation steps (Sev1 example):
1) Triage in Support: confirm incident details, customer impact, and gather logs/traces.
2) Notify stakeholders: post to #incidents (Slack) with summary and link to incident doc. Use template: "INCIDENT: {service} {severity} {summary} {impact}".
3) Page on-call runtime and eng-sre (pager duty): provide playbook-runner with API request id, trace ids, and sample payload.
4) Implement mitigation: trigger traffic reroute to fallback model variant or region; enable rate-limiting if overwhelmed.
5) Communicate: CSM coordinates customer comms; hourly updates until resolved.
6) Postmortem: within 72 hours, publish RCA doc and action items assigned with owners and target dates.

Escalation matrix (contacts):
- Support L1 channel: #support-l1 (Slack)
- Support L2 (on-call): support-l2@redwood.example.com
- SE escalation: se-oncall@redwood.example.com
- Eng runtime oncall: runtime-oncall@redwood.example.com (PagerDuty)
- CSM escalation lead: csm-lead@redwood.example.com

Support process and SLAs:
- Intake: All incoming customer issues must have a ticket created in Zendesk (or Salesforce Service Cloud) within 15 minutes of being reported.
- Initial response times (internal target):
  - Sev1: acknowledge in 15 minutes, begin mitigation within 30 minutes.
  - Sev2: acknowledge in 30 minutes, triage within 4 hours.
  - Sev3: acknowledge in 4 business hours, triage in 2 business days.
- Resolution expectations: set with customer at onboarding based on contract (standard is TTR targets: 8h for Sev2, 72h for Sev3).
- Ticket lifecycle fields (required): customer_priority, severity, impacted_routes, model_versions, tickets_link, incident_runbook_link, assigned_owner.

Known issues and workarounds (curated):
- Issue: Increased tokenization discrepancies causing slight output deviation after model update.
  - Symptoms: Deterministic prompts return different token boundaries resulting in subtle downstream parsing errors.
  - Workaround: Pin prior model minor version; apply post-tokenize normalization in client for the short term.
  - Owner: SE team.

- Issue: Occasional 502 from edge during autoscaling bursts when control-plane throttling occurs.
  - Symptoms: Short-lived 502 with retry-after header missing.
  - Workaround: Implement exponential backoff (start 200ms, factor 2, max 3 attempts) in client; enable small client-side circuit breaker.
  - Owner: eng-platform.

- Issue: Private deployment: slow KV cache warm-up after restart causing latency spike for first 100 requests.
  - Symptoms: 95th latency increases by 2-4x for first 5-10 minutes post-deploy.
  - Workaround: Run a synthetic warm-up job that replays recent prefixes (provided sample script) immediately after rollout.
  - Owner: eng-private-deployments.

- Issue: Embedding drift after batch-quantization across mixed CPU/GPU inference nodes.
  - Workaround: Reprocess embedding batch on uniform runtime (GPU/CPU) and add drift-tolerance threshold in similarity matching.

(Attach: short-example scripts and sample curl requests in the appendix or linked repo.)

Health checks & QBR materials:
- Recommended health-check cadence: weekly automated baseline (latency, error rate, token cost per request, cache hit rate), monthly review with customer engineers, quarterly business review with CSM/Product.
- Dashboard KPIs (minimum):
  - Request volume (per route), 95th/50th latency, error rate by code, tokens consumed (per route), cache hit ratio, model rollout adoption percent.
- QBR agenda (standard 60 minutes):
  1) Introductions & agenda (5m)
  2) Business goals & success metrics (10m)
  3) Operational health: metrics and recent incidents (15m)
  4) Feature roadmap & model recommendations (10m)
  5) Cost/optimization opportunities (10m)
  6) Open actions & next steps (10m)

QBR deliverables:
- One-pager with KPIs, action items, and recommended model/quantization changes.
- Updated onboarding checklist status and open risk register.

Templates and CLI snippets (examples):
- Ticket summary template:
  Title: [Sev{n}] {Service} - {Short summary}
  Body:
  - Impact: {number of users/endpoints}
  - Repro steps: {steps}
  - Recent deploys: {git sha}
  - Attachments: logs/traces/samples

- Warm-up script (example invocation):
  python tools/warmup_kv.py --target https://private-redwood.example.com --prefix-file recent-prefixes.txt --concurrency 8

- Retry/backoff example (pseudocode):
  for attempt in range(0, 3):
    resp = client.request(payload)
    if resp.status in [200, 201]:
      break
    sleep(0.2 * (2 ** attempt))

Operational playbooks and runbooks to reference:
- /confluence/eng-platform/runbooks/auto-scaling-tuning
- /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/runbooks/runtime-cache-warmup
- /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/incident-process

Postmortem and continuous improvement:
- After every Sev1/Sev2 impacting enterprise customer, create a postmortem within 72 hours. Include timeline, root cause, remediation, and preventative actions. Track action items in the central action tracker and review at the weekly SRE/CS sync.
